newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria sets $17 barrel oil price in 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria sets $17 barrel oil price in 97 budget.

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Saturday said it had taken a price of $17 per barrel as the basis for calculation of 1997 revenues.

"The projected revenue from oil sources in 1997 is 243 billion naira, an increase of 29 billion naira or 13.5 percent over the 1996 approved estimate of 214 billion naira," military ruler General Sani Abacha said in his 1997 budget broadcast.
Abacha said crude oil prices in 1996 had averaged $19.6 per barrel, against a budget forecast of $16 per barrel.
Over 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings come from crude oil exports, and it currently pumps around two million barrels of crude per day.
Abacha said non-oil revenue for 1997 is projected at 161 billion naira, an increase of 35 billion naira or 27.8 percent over the estimate approved for the previous year.
"Net revenue is therefore estimated at 404 billion naira. This represents an increase of 64 billion naira or 18.8 percent over the approved estimate of 340 billion naira in 1996," he said.

Abacha did not give an estimate for net expenditure, although he said capital expenditure would amount to 89 billion naira, recurrent expenditure 99 billion naira and 15 billion naira for servicing domestic debts.
He said $2.0 billion had been budgeted for external debt repayments, which would amount to 44 billion naira at the official exchange rate.
